author: Linnaeus, 1758
habitat: 섬의 채석장과 맨땅, 풀이 짧은 트인 곳

months.note: 국내에서 기록된 달이다(5월 가거도·어청도, 10월 홍도 등).

summary: 서해·남해 섬에서 드물게 관찰되는 길잃은새로, 2000년 5월 처음 기록된 뒤 봄(5월)과 가을(10월)에 몇 차례 기록되었다. 유라시아 북부를 가로질러 알래스카와 캐나다 동북부·그린란드까지 번식하며, 어느 번식지의 개체든 아프리카 사하라 이남으로 건너가 겨울을 난다. 돌이나 흙더미 위에 곧게 서서 꼬리를 까딱이다가 땅으로 내려가 딱정벌레 같은 곤충을 잡는다.

points.en: white forehead and supercilium above a black mask (male)
white tail with a black inverted T

sexes.male: 여름깃은 머리꼭대기와 등이 청회색이고 흰 눈썹선 아래로 눈을 지나는 검은 띠가 있으며, 날개는 검고 멱과 가슴은 담황색이다. 가을 털갈이 뒤에는 암컷과 비슷해진다.
sexes.female: 무늬 배치는 수컷과 같으나 윗면이 갈색을 띠고 날개는 흑갈색이며, 눈가의 검은 띠가 흐리거나 없다.

young: 갓 둥지를 떠난 어린새는 암수 모두 회갈색에서 담황갈색 바탕에 윗면에는 담색 반점, 가슴에는 갈색 얼룩이 있고 눈가의 검은 띠가 없다. 첫 겨울에는 암컷 겨울깃과 비슷해 암수를 가리기 어렵다.

art.subject: Northern Wheatear (Oenanthe oenanthe), adult male in breeding plumage, a spring migrant (May) on a Korean offshore island: crown, nape and back clean blue-grey; a narrow white band on the forehead continuing as a white supercilium; a black mask from the lores through the eye over the ear coverts; wings blackish without pale panels; throat and breast warm peachy-buff, fading to white on the belly and undertail coverts; rump and uppertail coverts white; tail white with black central feathers and a black terminal band forming a black inverted T. Bill black and slender; eye dark; legs black.
art.pose: standing upright on a rock with the tail slightly raised, side view
art.scene: grassy clifftop with short turf and scattered rocks on a Korean offshore island during spring migration (May), morning light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view standing upright on a rock, tail slightly raised: blue-grey crown, nape and back, white forehead and supercilium, black mask from the lores through the eye over the ear-coverts, black wings, buff throat and breast, white belly, white rump, white tail with a black centre and tip, slender black bill, long black legs

adult male breeding, in flight seen squarely from above: pointed black wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, blue-grey crown and back, white rump, white tail with a black inverted T formed by the central feathers and terminal band, head, body and tail in a straight line

adult female, side view standing upright on a rock: pale grey-brown upperparts, duller head pattern with a pale supercilium, darker brown wings, buff throat and breast, paler belly, white rump at the tail base, white tail with a black inverted T, black bill and legs
art.build: Small, compact, upright chat, a little larger than a sparrow, with a round head, short neck and fairly long black legs; stands tall, bobs and flicks its tail. Bill black, thin and straight, shorter than the head. Long wings: at rest the primaries project well beyond the tertials and the wingtips reach far down the short tail. Tail short and square. In flight the white rump and white tail sides with a black inverted T are striking, and the black wings contrast with the grey back.
avoid: Do not paint a sandy-brown back with pale wings — that is Isabelline Wheatear; the breeding male Northern has a blue-grey back and black wings.
Do not extend black onto the throat (male Desert Wheatear); the throat is peachy-buff.
Do not paint a mostly black tail; show white tail sides with a black inverted T.
Do not paint wing bars, streaks or a rufous back.
